clue.text: One goes over handy tips to catch train

definitions.note: the tips of the hand are the nails, and this tool is run over them

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them
a file is a line or train of people one behind another

explanation.surface: Someone fiddling with their fingertips while hurrying to catch a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy tips' is a play on hand: fingertips, where the nails are.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure tool is drawn across the ends of the fingers to shape the nails.

clue.text: Mould in bread, cut end off crust

indicators.note: cut here means the word for bread loses its final letter

parts.note: bread is slang for money, cash

indicators.note: the end taken off crust is its last letter

parts.note: last letter gives T

explanation.surface: Mould growing in bread: trim the end of the crust off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like the fungus in the bread, but it is the verb or noun for a shaping form. CASH loses its H, then T, the end of crust, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a mould, the shaped container into which molten material is poured to set.

clue.text: A piece of cake from party to go off without lid

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: losing its lid means the top, first letter of the word for go off, is removed

parts.note: eggs that addle go off, turn rotten

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a party with cake that has gone off because it had no lid.
explanation.walkthrough: ADDLE minus its first letter gives DDLE. A doddle is British slang for something very easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: Solid may drip when melted

indicators.note: melting a solid reshapes it, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A solid block might drip as it melts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' reads as an adjective but names a geometric solid.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a pyramid is a three-dimensional figure, a polyhedron with a polygon base.

clue.text: Djokovic, gutted about stupid visa, ended tennis competition

indicators.note: the outer letters go about, around, the shuffled visa
a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters give DC

indicators.note: a stupid arrangement of the letters of visa gives a new order

parts.note: up means over, ended, as in time is up

explanation.surface: Novak Djokovic, upset over a visa dispute, finished a tennis tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Djokovic's visa row before the 2022 Australian Open; 'gutted' looks like dismay but strips his name to its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davis Cup is the international team tournament in men's tennis.

clue.text: Prince with monsters making advances

parts.note: ogresses are female ogres, monsters

explanation.surface: A prince accompanied by monsters is getting somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To progress is to move forward, so it is a synonym for advances as a verb.

clue.text: See sign showing decay

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced see
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Look at the star sign that shows decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical term for tooth decay.

clue.text: Covering Virginia with sweat, ultimately perverted royal can

indicators.note: the shuffled letters cover, sit around, the state abbreviation
perverted means twisted, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of sweat

parts.note: last letter gives T
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A sweaty, depraved monarch is a disgrace to the state of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is American slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is slang for a toilet, a room or fixture for relieving oneself.

clue.text: Single American woman is out

parts.note: a means one, single
broad is dated American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: An unmarried American woman has gone out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abroad is away overseas, out of the country.

clue.text: Story books given to public library, initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: first letter gives P
first letter gives L
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Novels handed over to the public library at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a novel or film is its storyline, the sequence of events.

clue.text: Pulling leg? One might be used to stick on board

definitions.text: One might be used to stick on board

parts.note: drawing means pulling, as a cart
pin is slang for leg

explanation.surface: Teasing someone? That joke could be pinned on the noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling leg' suggests teasing; read literally it is drawing plus pin. A drawing pin is the British name for a thumbtack.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbtack is pushed in to fix paper to a noticeboard.

clue.text: Tone in empty bar: call from landlord to stop drinking outside?

indicators.note: the call goes outside, around, the emptied bar

parts.words: call from landlord to stop drinking
parts.note: time is the call a British pub landlord gives at closing

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: outer letters give BR

explanation.surface: A pub landlord calling closing time in an empty bar, with drinkers outside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub, 'Time!' is called when drinking must stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the quality or colour of a sound, its tone.

clue.text: Being off guard, catch a lot on the tube from one sitting

definitions.text: catch a lot on the tube from one sitting

indicators.note: off means bad, gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a watch is a guard or lookout

explanation.surface: Caught off guard and missing a train on the Underground while seated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tube' seems to be the London Underground, but it is television.
explanation.definitionFit: To binge-watch is to view many episodes of a TV series in one go.

clue.text: Grow part of wicket that's wearing at front

indicators.note: at front puts the word for wearing ahead of the cricket term

parts.note: in a hat means wearing a hat
the crease is a line marked on the cricket pitch near the wicket

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: grass grows on a part of the pitch worn bare at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the white line where the batter stands.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase is to become larger, a synonym of grow.

clue.text: Notes from singers on the radio

indicators.note: heard over the radio, the word is pronounced alike

parts.note: tenors are male singers

explanation.surface: Musical notes broadcast by vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks musical but means banknotes; a tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenners are ten-pound banknotes in British slang.

clue.text: Blow cover revealing criminal record

parts.note: a rap is a blow or knock
a sheet is a bed cover

explanation.surface: A blown cover exposes someone's past offences.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap sheet is American slang for a police record of past arrests and convictions.

clue.text: One with speed wrestling around ring in bout

indicators.note: wrestling around means tumbling about, so the numeral, speed and the ring letter are all rearranged together

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A fast wrestler fighting around the ring in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bout' looks like a wrestling contest but means a spell, as in a bout of flu.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a spell or occurrence of something, like a bout of illness.

clue.text: Make love with partner after what starts off like mad

indicators.note: the partner comes after the letter from like

parts.note: to do is to make
O is zero, love in tennis

indicators.note: the start of like is its first letter

parts.note: first letter gives L
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A romantic instruction: get together with your partner after something starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Doolally is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doolally means crazy or out of one's mind in British informal speech.

clue.text: Short bloke with hard dog

indicators.note: short means the word for bloke loses its last letter

parts.note: a bloke is a man
stiff means hard, rigid

explanation.surface: A short man with a tough dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Climber, perhaps one following main course to summit, shortly

parts.note: sweet is British for dessert, the course after the main

indicators.note: shortly cuts the last letter of the word for summit

parts.note: a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: A mountaineer, after a main course, heads for the summit soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a flowering plant that climbs by tendrils, an example of a climber.

clue.text: Wear warm clothes with cuff down? On the contrary

parts.note: a rap is a cuff, a light blow
the contrary of down is up

explanation.surface: Bundling up with your shirt cuffs pulled down, or perhaps rolled up instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' turns down into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up is to dress warmly against cold weather.

clue.text: AC/DC quiet round piano playing piece

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, bi
sh is a call for quiet
O is round in shape
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: The rock band AC/DC playing quietly around a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AC/DC' suggests the rock band; it is slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a chess piece, one of the pieces used in playing the game.

clue.text: Shallow vessel to move across under bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue, the camera move goes under the bottom

parts.note: a bed is a bottom, as of the sea or river
to pan a camera is to move it across a scene

explanation.surface: A shallow boat moving across beneath something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but means a container; and its use is on a bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedpan is a shallow receptacle used by a bedridden patient as a toilet.

clue.text: Dropped teacup, hard to get replacement

indicators.note: replacement means the letters are placed differently

explanation.surface: Someone dropped a teacup and finds a replacement hard to get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' looks like it belongs to the teacup, but it means descended by parachute.
explanation.definitionFit: To parachute is to drop from an aircraft by canopy, so parachuted means dropped.

clue.text: Cold butter and jam

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: A breakfast of cold butter and jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is the spread, but read it as one who butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to jam or pack things tightly into a space.

clue.text: Point made with carbon copy

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: A point made with a carbon copy of a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland or promontory, a point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Might mark cryptic clues

parts.note: M stands for the German mark, the old currency

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The setter might grade cryptic clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' poses as a verb but is a noun for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical strength or power, the noun sense of might.

clue.text: Peter out with Rod and Jack on this?

parts.note: to flag is to tire, peter out
a pole is a rod

explanation.surface: Peter is out with two friends, Rod and Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter, Rod and Jack all look like names. The Union Jack is the British flag, which flies on one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is where a Union Jack or other flag is hoisted.
